pkgmetadata.longdescription: rmtfs serves the EFS (modem file system) of Qualcomm platforms to the modem processor over QRTR. The modem asks for its partitions and NV items through QMI, and rmtfs answers by reading and writing either the raw partitions exported by the kernel (devices named qcom_rmtfs_mem*, selected with -P) or a directory of images (selected with -o). It is normally started together with the modem remoteproc, and on mainline kernels the -s option ties the modem's lifecycle to the daemon. rmtfs.service runs with raw partitions and rmtfs-dir.service with the /var/lib/rmtfs image directory; both are started on demand by the udev rule that watches for the qcom_rmtfs_mem device.
